o: We may reduce tower heights (never increase) so the array is non-decreasing up to a peak and non-increasing after; maximize the resulting sum. For a fixed peak i, the best arrangement caps every element left of i at a non-decreasing envelope ending at heights[i], and symmetrically on the right. Example [5,3,4,1,1] → peak 0, [5,3,3,1,1], sum 13. With n ≤ 1000, an O(n²) sweep per peak passes comfortably; a monotonic-stack technique computes all left/right envelopes in O(n) total.
k: Fixing the peak i, the optimal left part caps each prefix element at a running envelope bounded by heights[i]; same mirrored on the right.
Answer = max over i of L[i] + R[i] − heights[i], where L/R are best mountain-half sums ending/starting at i.
A monotonic stack of (height, count, segment-sum) maintains capped staircase sums in amortized O(1) per element.

a.i: For each candidate peak i, walk left keeping a running cap (each element contributes min(h[j], cap), then cap = min(cap, h[j])), and likewise rightward; sum both halves minus the double-counted peak. O(n²) but dead simple.
s: For each i: sweep left with running cap, sweep right with running cap.
a.t: O(n²) — two linear sweeps per peak.

a.i: Maintain a stack of segments (height, count) representing a strictly increasing staircase; its total is the best non-decreasing sum ending at the current index. When a new (smaller-or-equal) height arrives, pop taller-or-equal segments and re-price them at the new height. Compute L left-to-right and R right-to-left; answer = max(L[i] + R[i] − h[i]).
s: calc(h): for each x, pop segments with height ≥ x, merge counts, push (x, count·x); record running total as L[i].
Do the same on the reversed array for R.
a.t: O(n) — each element is pushed and popped from the stack at most once per direction.
a.sp: O(n) for stacks and the L/R arrays.

w: For n ≤ 1000 the brute force is perfectly acceptable and easier to defend; the stack version is required for the hard variant (2866, n up to 1e5). Pitfalls: subtracting heights[i] once when combining L and R (double-counted peak), using 32-bit sums (values up to 1e9 · 1e3), and the stack pop condition must be ≥ (equal heights merge). Follow-up: solve 2866 with the same code, or return the actual height assignment.
